newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Telmex rides local momentum.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Telmex rides local momentum.

text.p: Mexican telephone company Telefonos de Mexico kept riding the momentum of an upbeat local market, making its American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) the fifth most active issue in terms of volume on the New York Stock Exchange, traders said Thursday.
"There's a lot of momentum in the (Mexican) market right now," said one dealer.
Mexican stocks surged higher in morning trade as foreign investors flooded the market in light of year-low U.S. long bond yields and a cheaper peso.
Telmex saw its ADR trading 11/16 higher at 55-3/16, surpassing its year high of 54-7/8 in midday trading.

Among other Latin American ADRs, Brazil's telephone holding company Telebras SA was down 3-5/16 at 146-1/2, and Venezuela's Corimon SACA was up 13/16 at 8-1/16 a day after reporting lower first-quarter earnings.
European ADRs were also active, with Sweden's telecommunications equipment company Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson down 9/16 at 45-3/8 and Royal Dutch Petroleum up 6/16 at 55-13/16.
France's engineering company Alcatel Alsthom rose 15/16 at 26-15/16 after reporting that its first-half sales were up 17 percent at 86.92 billion francs.
"It had good numbers," said one dealer, adding that it was one of the more active ADRs of the region.
Advancers led decliners 270 to 234 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group was up 0.25 percent on a volume of 46.3 million ADRs.
ADRs allow U.S. trade of foreign shares.
